newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Deputy Prime Minister Samak Sundaravej says he will ask the prime minister to call a two-day extraordinary session of Parliament to debate the Bangkok Bank of Commerce loans scandal. He says the debate will help the public realise just who left behind a dirty mess in the House and caused public confusion. (THE NATION)

- Highway police have proposed a legislative amendment that metes out punishment to the owners of trucks weighing over the legal limit of 21-tonnes to be driven on the roads. The current law only administers legal action against the truck drivers, most of whom are not the truck owners but are hired to transport the goods. Police and the Highway Department are drafting an amendment for the Highway Act so the punishment will be expanded to cover the truck owners as well. (BANGKOK POST)

- Having secured fresh support from 133 non-governmental organisations, the Forum of the Poor will exert more pressure on the government, in the hope to bring about quick and effective solutions to the grievances of protesting farmers and workers. Representatives of the 133 NGOs, including hundreds of lecturers, will join Forum of the Poor leaders in submitting a memorandum to Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh at Government House tomorrow. (BANGKOK POST)

- National Petrochemicals Plc will postpone its three downstream petrochemical projects, worth a combined investment of 14 billion baht, despite the earlier signing of two memorandums of understanding with foreign companies for joint investments. The company says that it has decided to put the projects on hold due to the country's economic doldrums. As a result of oversupply in the upstream petrochemical sector, the downstream projects, which will produce polyethylene resins, will be delayed for more than one year. (THE NATION)

- Thailand is waiting on the sidelines hoping that the "unique geographic sourcing" of goods will be registered as an intellectual property in the future because it has a wide range of products with special characteristics. The European Union's attempt to register the unique geographic sourcing of wine under the World Trade Organisation failed to go through because of objections from significant members, namely the U.S., Australia, Canada and New Zealand. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Esso Standard (Thailand) Ltd will spend 10 billion baht on building an aromatics plant in Thailand as part of its plan for integrated petroleum operations. The move came one day after Chevron Ltd of the United States and the Petroleum Authority of Thailand announced a similar venture. (BANGKOK POST)
